subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THREE FINDINGS ON THE TERNARY-DIAMOND FAMILY, one of them a prediction that was stated before the build and then held exactly.

(1) THE TERNARY LEVER AND THE SURPLUS-COPY CLASS ARE ONE JOINT LEVER, NOT TWO AXES, AND MEASURING EITHER ALONE PRICES IT WRONG. A residual of the shape 'target has N extra forward branches, we have N extra register copies, and the instruction counts are therefore EQUAL' is a single mechanism seen from two sides, and the equal count is an accident of the two classes cancelling. Measured on setWorldParms: the outer-guard ternary probed ALONE against the original baseline cost four instructions, moved the multiset only 32t -> 20t, lost fuzzy, and was reverted by the previous run as a bad trade. The SAME character-for-character edit, applied after the surplus-copy class had been removed first, took the multiset 22t -> 5t. Reversing the order changes the verdict from 'reject' to 'the largest single structural win in the function'. This is the two-variable-axis discipline (AGENTS.md residual-work discipline 6) instantiated for branch architecture: when a target-only branch class and an ours-only copy class have equal cardinality in the same clusters, they are ONE lever and MUST be probed jointly before either is parked.

COROLLARY, AND THE EXPENSIVE HALF: EQUAL INSTRUCTION COUNT IS NOT THE RECOLOR PRECONDITION - EQUAL INSTRUCTION SHAPE IS. The previous run declined this lever explicitly to protect a 843/843 count parity, on the correct general principle that a WebFrank recolor rule needs identical instruction shape. But that parity was composed of 10 surplus fmr against 10 missing b - twenty words that no recolor rule can ever touch. Breaking the parity to 843/844 while emptying the target-only opcode set left the function ONE word from shape identity. When arbitrating a count-parity trade, ask which words the parity is made of; a parity built from two cancelling error classes is worth nothing.

(2) A TERNARY ARM EMITS ITS BRANCH EVEN WHEN THE ARM IS EMPTY; AN EMPTY IF-ARM DOES NOT. This is why no statement-level spelling can produce the target's `bcond ->else / b ->join` pair when one arm is a no-op. claim.law.IT_empty-bodied-if-elides-its-own-comparison.20260901.v1 and claim.law.MB_empty-then-with-else-also-folds-and-ternary-count-cost-is-per-function.20260901.v1 establish that MWCC's front end folds an empty if-arm (with or without an else) before codegen, so the arm never reaches the branch generator. A ternary arm is an expression block that is emitted unconditionally, so when register coalescing makes the arm's copy a no-op the block degenerates to exactly the `b ->join` the target shows. Operationally: if the target materialises an empty arm as a branch, the ternary is the ONLY carrier, and the surviving question is never 'which spelling' but 'which register the result lands in'.

(3) THE NEW MECHANISM, STATED AS A PREDICTION AND CONFIRMED. MWCC coalesces a ternary's result with its ASSIGNMENT DESTINATION only at sites where that destination has already been assigned earlier in its declaration scope; at the FIRST assignment site in the scope it instead allocates a fresh scratch register, which makes both identity arms non-empty and costs one surplus copy. Consequently the defect appears EXACTLY ONCE PER DECLARATION SCOPE, at that scope's textually first consumer, and is independent of the source spelling at the failing site.

THE EVIDENCE IS A CONTROLLED TEST, not an inference from one function. setWorldParms has one declaration scope for `sc/lo/hi` and showed exactly one failing group, its first. MBNewPsysDescrip initially received the same edit with `sc/lo/hi` declared in EACH of its two `f32 x3, x2, x1, x0;` block scopes, and showed exactly TWO failing groups - the first group of each block (@0x60c and @0xa9c) - while the other three reproduced the target byte-shape. The prediction 'collapse the two declaration scopes into one function-scope declaration and exactly one failure will remain' was written down before the build; measured result: multiset 2t -> 1t, insns 795 -> 794, the @0xa9c cluster gone and @0x60c unchanged.

WHAT THIS EXTENDS. claim.law.GW_block-scope-splits-a-coalesced-copy-but-a-same-scope-copy-folds.20260901.v1 names block scope as the lever for the inverse (target-has-the-copy) polarity and lists as a NON-cure (b) that 'splitting a declaration-with-initializer into a bare declaration plus an assignment is NEUTRAL'. That non-cure does NOT generalise: here precisely that split, when it also WIDENS the scope so one variable serves several consumers, removed a surplus copy and was the difference between two failures and one. GW's own discriminator already predicts this - the two forms must differ in scope AND live-range shape, not merely in spelling - so read non-cure (b) as scoped to a same-scope split, and read the widening split as a live lever in both polarities.

FOUR MEASURED NON-CURES AT THE FAILING SITE, so the next lane does not respend them (all on setWorldParms, all leaving the structure untouched): declaration order `f32 lo, hi, sc;` is BYTE-IDENTICAL; declaring sc/lo/hi before t0..t3 moves real 497 -> 501 with the structure unchanged; moving the real assignment into the inner else arm, `lo = (t3 < lo) ? lo : ((t3 > hi) ? hi : (hi = t3));`, gives real 557 unchanged structurally; and forcing a read of hi's home with a comma operator, `lo = (t3 < lo) ? lo : (hi = (t3 > hi) ? hi : t3, hi);`, is strictly worse (insns 848, multiset 5t) because it reloads hi from the pool. The pragma axis is null in BOTH directions: `#pragma opt_lifetimes on` scoped around the function is NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL (the default already behaves as `on`) and `off` is worse (insns 847, multiset 6t). Since the mechanism is a first-definition property of the allocator rather than a property of the source at the failing site, spelling probes AT that site are predicted dead; a cure, if one exists, must give the destination an earlier definition in the same scope.

CLASSIFICATION NOTE: the surviving residual is a surplus INSTRUCTION, not a register field, so it is NOT WebFrank-eligible - the postprocessor recolors and permutes words, it cannot delete one. A function reduced to this residual is one genuine row from CLEAN-RENAMING but is not there, and must not be reported as recolor-ready.
